source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which cranial nerve is tested by asking the client to smell coffee with eyes closed?
questions.rationale: CN I mediates smell; loss is anosmia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Cranial nerves (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: Olfactory ... Smell ... Anosmia (absence of smell

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client cannot close his right eye or smile on the right side after a viral illness. Which nerve is affected?
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy affects CN VII, controlling facial expression and taste of the anterior 2/3 of the tongue.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Cranial nerves (PDF p. 334)
questions.quote: Bell's palsy; ageusia (loss of sense of taste) on the anterior 2/3 of the ton uc.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sympathetic stimulation causes which effect?
questions.rationale: SNS: everything high and fast except GI/GU; pupils and bronchi dilate, heart speeds up.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Autonomic nervous system (PDF p. 336)
questions.quote: DILATE • Pupils • Bronchial Tree

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Mang Lito is scheduled for an EEG tomorrow morning and asks how to prepare. The nurse tells him to:
questions.rationale: Clean hair improves electrode contact; avoid caffeine and stimulants beforehand. The test does not shock.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 EEG (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: Hair shampoo to remove oils and dirt which may interfere with transmission of electrical impulses

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The doctor is about to insert the spinal needle for a lumbar tap on Aling Nena. How should the nurse position her?
questions.rationale: The fetal position arches the back and widens the intervertebral spaces for needle entry.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Lumbar puncture (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: lateral recumbent position with back arched; head and knees flexed on chest

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After lumbar puncture, to reduce the risk of headache the client should:
questions.rationale: Lying flat for several hours and fluids help prevent CSF-leak headache.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Lumbar puncture (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: Lie flat in bed for 6 - 8 hours (may turn to sides). • Encourage fluids if not contraindicated.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: CSF analysis shows low glucose and high protein. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Low CSF glucose suggests infection; high protein suggests infection or tumor.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Normal CSF values (PDF p. 341)
questions.quote: Low glucose level indicates infection.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is the single most sensitive indicator of changing neurologic status?
questions.rationale: LOC changes earliest and most sensitively reflect neurologic deterioration.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Neurologic assessment (PDF p. 343)
questions.quote: It is the single most sensitive indicator of changes in the neurologic status ofa client.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A head-injury client opens eyes to pain, moans, and withdraws from pain. His GCS is:
questions.rationale: Eyes to pain 2 + incomprehensible sounds 2 + withdrawal 4 = 8; 8 or lower suggests severe injury.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Glasgow Coma Scale (PDF p. 356)
questions.quote: 4— flexion withdrawal

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client falls when standing with feet together and eyes closed. This positive Romberg test suggests a problem with the:
questions.rationale: Romberg assesses equilibrium (cerebellar/proprioceptive function); slight swaying is normal, falling is positive.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Motor function (PDF p. 345)
questions.quote: If the client falls. this is positive Romberg that indicates cerebellar function impairment.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Passive neck flexion causes the client to flex his hips. This is:
questions.rationale: Brudzinski's sign indicates meningeal irritation; Kernig's is pain on leg extension with hip flexed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Meningeal irritation (PDF p. 346)
questions.quote: Passively flex the neck, spontaneous flexion of the hips occurs.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client understands speech but cannot form words after a stroke. This is:
questions.rationale: Broca's area (left frontal) controls speech production; damage causes expressive aphasia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Language and speech (PDF p. 347)
questions.quote: Impairment of the Broca's area results to expressive or motor aphasia

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is often the earliest sign of increasing intracranial pressure?
questions.rationale: Restlessness and subtle LOC changes come first; pupil fixation, Cushing's triad and posturing are late.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Increased ICP (PDF p. 348)
questions.quote: Restlessness. Is the initial sign of increased ICP.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Cushing's triad of increased ICP includes:
questions.rationale: Rising systolic BP with widened pulse pressure, bradycardia and slow/irregular respirations.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Cushing's triad (PDF p. 348)
questions.quote: Widening of pulse pressure. It is more than 40 mmHg.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with increased ICP is best positioned with the head of bed at:
questions.rationale: Elevating 15–30 degrees with the head midline promotes venous drainage; extreme positions raise ICP.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Increased ICP management (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: The HOB elevation is 15 to 30 degree, maximum of 45 degree.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which activity should a client with increased ICP avoid?
questions.rationale: Valsalva, vomiting, over-suctioning, restraints and bending raise ICP.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Increased ICP management (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: Valsalva maneuver, e.g. straining at stool

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client receiving IV mannitol for cerebral edema needs close monitoring of:
questions.rationale: Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic; monitor hourly output and BP for hypotension.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Pharmacotherapy for ICP (PDF p. 350)
questions.quote: Check hourly urine output.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A fixed, dilated pupil develops in a client whose pupils were reactive. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: A newly fixed, dilated pupil signals herniation and is a neurologic emergency.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Pupillary reflexes (PDF p. 346)
questions.quote: A fixed and dilated pupil in a client who has had previously reactive pupils is a neurologic emergency.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which posture signals brainstem involvement and poor prognosis?
questions.rationale: Decerebrate (rigid extension) indicates brainstem damage; decorticate (flexion) indicates involvement above the midbrain.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Brainstem impairment (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: This indicates involvement of the brainstem. This signals poor prognosis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A 25-year-old jeepney driver has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure in the clinic waiting area. The nurse's best action is to:
questions.rationale: Protect from injury, side-lying for airway, loosen clothing; never restrain or force objects into the mouth.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Seizure management (PDF p. 351)
questions.quote: Turn the client to the side.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has brief staring spells with lip-smacking that end in seconds, then resumes play. This is:
questions.rationale: Absence seizures: no aura, blank stare, automatisms, 10–20 seconds, common in children; ethosuximide is used.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Petit mal seizures (PDF p. 351)
questions.quote: It is characterized by blank facial expression and automatism like lip — chewing

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: IV phenytoin should be mixed only with:
questions.rationale: Phenytoin precipitates in dextrose solutions; dilute and flush with normal saline.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Hydantoins (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: It should be diluted with normal saline solution. Dextrose solution should not be used because of drug precipitation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the therapeutic serum range of phenytoin?
questions.rationale: Phenytoin's therapeutic level is 10–20 mcg/mL.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Hydantoins (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: The therapeutic serum level of Phenytoin is 10 to 20 mcg./ml.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on long-term phenytoin should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Phenytoin causes gingival hyperplasia; brush with a soft brush, massage gums, see the dentist. Never stop abruptly.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Phenytoin therapy (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: To prevent gingival hyperplasia (overgrowth of gum tissues — reddened gums that bleed easily)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client asks why her urine turned pinkish on phenytoin. The nurse explains:
options: It is a harmless drug effect
questions.rationale: Phenytoin can cause pinkish-red or red-brown urine; this is harmless.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Hydantoin side effects (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: Phenytoin causes pinkish red or reddish — brmvn discoloration of urine. This is a harmless side effect.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why must anticonvulsants be withdrawn gradually?
questions.rationale: Abrupt withdrawal can trigger rebound seizures and status epilepticus.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Hydantoins (PDF p. 353)
questions.quote: Withdraw anticonvulsant drugs gradually to prevent status epilepticus.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug is given IV to stop status epilepticus?
questions.rationale: IV benzodiazepines (lorazepam, diazepam) are first-line for status epilepticus; lorazepam no faster than 2 mg/min.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Benzodiazepines (PDF p. 354)
questions.quote: Lorazepam is used to control status epilepticus. Infusion rate should not exceed 2mg/min.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on valproic acid needs periodic monitoring of:
questions.rationale: Valproic acid is hepatotoxic; it is also teratogenic (neural tube defects).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Valproate (PDF p. 355)
questions.quote: Valproic acid is hcpatotoxic so liver enzymes should be monitored.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A pregnant woman on anticonvulsants should take which supplement daily?
questions.rationale: Anticonvulsants deplete folate and some are teratogenic; daily folate is advised.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Anticonvulsants and pregnancy (PDF p. 355)
questions.quote: Anticonvulsant drugs cause loss of folate (folic acid) in pregnant women; thus daily folate supplements should be taken.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which environment helps during a migraine attack?
questions.rationale: Migraines involve photophobia and phonophobia; a quiet, dark room helps.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Migraine (PDF p. 356)
questions.quote: Provide quiet, dark environment.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sumatriptan should be avoided in a client with:
questions.rationale: Triptans cause vasoconstriction and are contraindicated in hypertension and coronary disease.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Triptans (PDF p. 357)
questions.quote: Imitrex is contraindicated in hypertension, renal and hepatic impairment.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is typical of a left-hemisphere stroke?
questions.rationale: Left CVA: right-sided paralysis, aphasia, slow cautious behavior; right CVA: left paralysis, spatial deficits, impulsivity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Left vs. right CVA (PDF p. 358)
questions.quote: Ri ht hemi le ia ... Aphasia: expressive, receptive

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A stroke client has left homonymous hemianopsia. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Approach and place items on the unaffected visual side and teach him to scan by turning his head.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Hemianopsia (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: Approach the client from the unaffected side of the visual field.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should the nurse communicate with a client who has expressive aphasia?
questions.rationale: Give time to respond, one word or command at a time, and reinforce success.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 10 Care of client with aphasia (PDF p. 359)
questions.quote: Allow the client to verbalize, no matter how long it takes him.
